verses.zh: 以色列王约哈斯的儿子约阿施第二年，犹大王约阿施的儿子亚玛谢登基。
verses.en: In the second year of the reign of Israel’s King Joash son of Joahaz,[NOTE:1] Joash’s[NOTE:2] son Amaziah became king over Judah.
notes: The name Joahaz is an alternate form of Jehoahaz.
The referent here is Joash of Judah (see 12:21), not Joash of Israel, mentioned earlier in the verse.

verses.zh: 他登基的时候年二十五岁，在耶路撒冷作王二十九年。他母亲名叫约耶但，是耶路撒冷人。
verses.en: He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem.[NOTE:1] His mother[NOTE:2] was Jehoaddan, who was from Jerusalem.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “the name of his mother.”

verses.zh: 亚玛谢行耶和华眼中看为正的事，但不如他祖大卫，乃效法他父约阿施一切所行的；
verses.en: He did what the Lord approved,[NOTE:1] but not like David his ancestor had done. He followed the example of his father Joash.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “he did what was proper in the eyes of the Lord.”
Heb “according to all which Joash his father had done, he did.”

verses.zh: 只是邱坛还没有废去，百姓仍在那里献祭烧香。
verses.en: But the high places were not eliminated; the people continued to offer sacrifices and burn incense on the high places.

verses.zh: 国一坚定，就把杀他父王的臣仆杀了，
verses.en: When he had secured control of the kingdom,[NOTE:1] he executed the servants who had assassinated his father.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “when the kingdom was secure in his hand.”
Heb “he struck down his servants, the ones who had struck down the king, his father.”

verses.zh: 却没有治死杀王之人的儿子，是照摩西律法书上耶和华所吩咐的说：「不可因子杀父，也不可因父杀子，各人要为本身的罪而死。」
verses.en: But he did not execute the sons of the assassins. He obeyed the Lord’s commandment as recorded in the scroll of the law of Moses, “Fathers must not be put to death for what their sons do,[NOTE:1] and sons must not be put to death for what their fathers do.[NOTE:2] A man must be put to death only for his own sin.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “on account of sons.”
Heb “on account of fathers.”
This law is recorded in Deut 24:16.

verses.zh: 亚玛谢在盐谷杀了以东人一万，又攻取了西拉，改名叫约帖，直到今日。
verses.en: He defeated[NOTE:1] 10,000 Edomites in the Salt Valley; he captured Sela in battle and renamed it Joktheel, a name it has retained to this very day.
notes: Or “struck down.”

verses.zh: 那时，亚玛谢差遣使者去见耶户的孙子约哈斯的儿子以色列王约阿施，说：「你来，我们二人相见于战场。」
verses.en: Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel. He said, “Come, let’s meet face to face.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “let us look at each other [in the] face.” The expression refers here to meeting in battle. See v. 11.

verses.zh: 以色列王约阿施差遣使者去见犹大王亚玛谢，说：「黎巴嫩的蒺藜差遣使者去见黎巴嫩的香柏树，说：将你的女儿给我儿子为妻。后来黎巴嫩有一个野兽经过，把蒺藜践踏了。
verses.en: King Jehoash of Israel sent this message back to King Amaziah of Judah, “A thornbush in Lebanon sent this message to a cedar in Lebanon, ‘Give your daughter to my son as a wife.’ Then a wild animal[NOTE:1] of Lebanon came by and trampled down the thorn.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the animal of the field.”

Judah is the thorn in the allegory. Amaziah’s success has deceived him into thinking he is on the same level as the major powers in the area (symbolized by the cedar). In reality he is not capable of withstanding an attack by a real military power such as Israel (symbolized by the wild animal).

verses.zh: 你打败了以东人就心高气傲，你以此为荣耀，在家里安居就罢了，为何要惹祸，使自己和犹大国一同败亡呢？」
verses.en: You thoroughly defeated Edom,[NOTE:1] and it has gone to your head![NOTE:2] Gloat over your success,[NOTE:3] but stay in your palace. Why bring calamity on yourself? Why bring down yourself and Judah along with you?”[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “you have indeed defeated Edom.”
Heb “and your heart has lifted you up.”
Heb “be glorified.”
Heb “Why get involved in calamity and fall, you and Judah with you?”

verses.zh: 亚玛谢却不肯听这话。于是以色列王约阿施上来，在犹大的伯．示麦与犹大王亚玛谢相见于战场。
verses.en: But Amaziah would not heed the warning,[NOTE:1] so King Jehoash of Israel attacked.[NOTE:2] He and King Amaziah of Judah met face to face[NOTE:3] in Beth Shemesh of Judah.
notes: Heb “did not listen.”
Heb “went up.”
Heb “looked at each other [in the] face.”

verses.zh: 犹大人败在以色列人面前，各自逃回家里去了。
verses.en: Judah was defeated by Israel, and each man ran back home.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and Judah was struck down before Israel and they fled, each to his tent.”

verses.zh: 以色列王约阿施在伯．示麦擒住亚哈谢的孙子、约阿施的儿子犹大王亚玛谢，就来到耶路撒冷，拆毁耶路撒冷的城墙，从以法莲门直到角门共四百肘，
verses.en: King Jehoash of Israel captured King Amaziah of Judah, son of Jehoash son of Ahaziah, in Beth Shemesh. He[NOTE:1] attacked[NOTE:2] Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate—a distance of about 600 feet.[NOTE:3]
notes: The MT has the plural form of the verb, but the final vav (ו) is virtually dittographic. The word that immediately follows in the Hebrew text begins with a yod (י). The form should be emended to the singular, which is consistent in number with the verb (“he broke down”) that follows.
Heb “came to.”
Heb “400 cubits.” The standard cubit in the OT is assumed by most authorities to be about 18 inches (45 cm) long.

verses.zh: 又将耶和华殿里与王宫府库里所有的金银和器皿都拿了去，并带人去为质，就回撒马利亚去了。
verses.en: He took away all the gold and silver, all the items found in the Lord’s temple and in the treasuries of the royal palace, and some hostages.[NOTE:1] Then he went back to Samaria.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the sons of the pledges.”
For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

verses.zh: 约阿施其余所行的事和他的勇力，并与犹大王亚玛谢争战的事，都写在以色列诸王记上。
verses.en: The rest of the events of Jehoash’s[NOTE:1] reign, including all his accomplishments and his successful war with King Amaziah of Judah, are recorded in the scroll called the Annals of the Kings of Israel.[NOTE:2]
notes: Jehoash and Joash are alternate forms of the same name.

Heb “As for the rest of the events of Jehoash, and all which he did and his strength, [and] how he fought with Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?”

verses.zh: 约阿施与他列祖同睡，葬在撒马利亚，以色列诸王的坟地里。他儿子耶罗波安接续他作王。
verses.en: Jehoash passed away[NOTE:1] and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel. His son Jeroboam replaced him as king.
notes: Heb “lay down with his fathers.”

verses.zh: 以色列王约哈斯的儿子约阿施死后，犹大王约阿施的儿子亚玛谢又活了十五年。
verses.en: King Amaziah son of Joash of Judah lived for 15 years after the death of King Jehoash son of Jehoahaz of Israel.

verses.zh: 亚玛谢其余的事都写在犹大列王记上。
verses.en: The rest of the events of Amaziah’s reign are recorded in the scroll called the Annals of the Kings of Judah.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “As for the rest of the events of Amaziah, are they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Judah?”

verses.zh: 耶路撒冷有人背叛亚玛谢，他就逃到拉吉；叛党却打发人到拉吉将他杀了。
verses.en: Conspirators plotted against him in Jerusalem,[NOTE:1] so he fled to Lachish. But they sent assassins after him,[NOTE:2] and they killed him there.
notes: Heb “and they conspired against him [with] a conspiracy in Jerusalem.”
Heb “and they sent after him to Lachish.”

verses.zh: 人就用马将他的尸首驮到耶路撒冷，葬在大卫城他列祖的坟地里。
verses.en: His body was carried back by horses,[NOTE:1] and he was buried in Jerusalem with his ancestors in the City of David.
notes: Heb “and they carried him on horses.”

verses.zh: 犹大众民立亚玛谢的儿子亚撒利雅（又名乌西雅）接续他父作王，那时他年十六岁。
verses.en: All the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in his father Amaziah’s place.

verses.zh: 亚玛谢与他列祖同睡之后，亚撒利雅收回以拉他仍归犹大，又重新修理。
verses.en: Azariah[NOTE:1] built up Elat and restored it to Judah after the king[NOTE:2] had passed away.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Azariah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
This must refer to Amaziah.
Heb “lay with his fathers.”

verses.zh: 犹大王约阿施的儿子亚玛谢十五年，以色列王约阿施的儿子耶罗波安在撒马利亚登基，作王四十一年。
verses.en: In the fifteenth year of the reign of Judah’s King Amaziah son of Joash, Jeroboam son of Joash became king over Israel. He reigned for 41 years in Samaria.[NOTE:1]
notes: For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

verses.zh: 他行耶和华眼中看为恶的事，不离开尼八的儿子耶罗波安使以色列人陷在罪里的一切罪。
verses.en: He did evil in the sight of[NOTE:1] the Lord; he did not repudiate[NOTE:2] the sinful ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat who encouraged Israel to sin.
notes: Heb “in the eyes of.”
Heb “turn away from all.”

verses.zh: 他收回以色列边界之地，从哈马口直到亚拉巴海，正如耶和华―以色列的　神藉他仆人迦特希弗人亚米太的儿子先知约拿所说的。
verses.en: He restored the border of Israel from Lebo Hamath[NOTE:1] in the north to the sea of the rift valley[NOTE:2] in the south,[NOTE:3] just as in the message from the Lord God of Israel that he had announced through his servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet from Gath Hepher.
notes: Or “entrance of Hamath” (so NASB and cf. KJV). This may be a site some 44 miles north of Damascus (see T. R. Hobbs, 2 Kings [WBC], 182).
The “sea of the rift valley” is the Dead Sea.
The phrases “in the north” and “in the south” are added in the translation for clarification.

verses.zh: 因为耶和华看见以色列人甚是艰苦，无论困住的、自由的都没有了，也无人帮助以色列人。
verses.en: The Lord saw Israel’s intense suffering;[NOTE:1] everyone was weak and incapacitated and Israel had no deliverer.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “for the Lord saw the very bitter affliction of Israel.” This translation assumes an emendation of מֹרֶה (moreh), which is meaningless here, to הַמַּר (hammar), the adjective “bitter” functioning attributively with the article prefixed. This emendation is supported by the LXX, Syriac Peshitta, and Vulgate. Another option would be מַר הוּא (mar huʾ), “it was bitter.”

Heb “[there was] none but the restrained, and [there was] none but the abandoned, and there was no deliverer for Israel.” On the meaning of the terms עָצוּר (ʿatsur) and עָזוּב (ʿazur), see the note at 1 Kgs 14:10.

verses.zh: 耶和华并没有说要将以色列的名从天下涂抹，乃藉约阿施的儿子耶罗波安拯救他们。
verses.en: The Lord had not decreed that he would blot out Israel’s memory[NOTE:1] from under heaven,[NOTE:2] so he delivered them through Jeroboam son of Joash.
notes: Heb “name.”

The phrase “from under heaven” adds emphasis to the verb “blot out” and suggest total annihilation. For other examples of the verb מָחָה (makhah), “blot out,” combined with “from under heaven,” see Exod 17:14; Deut 9:14; 25:19; 29:20.

verses.zh: 耶罗波安其余的事，凡他所行的和他的勇力，他怎样争战，怎样收回大马士革和先前属犹大的哈马归以色列，都写在以色列诸王记上。
verses.en: The rest of the events of Jeroboam’s reign, including all his accomplishments, his military success in restoring Israelite control over Damascus and Hamath, are recorded in the scroll called the Annals of the Kings of Israel.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “As for the rest of the events of Jeroboam, and all which he did and his strength, [and] how he fought and how he restored Damascus and Hamath to Judah in Israel, are they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?” The phrase “to Judah” is probably not original; it may be a scribal addition by a Judahite scribe who was trying to link Jeroboam’s conquests with the earlier achievements of David and Solomon, who ruled in Judah. The Syriac Peshitta has simply “to Israel.” M. Cogan and H. Tadmor (II Kings [AB], 162) offer this proposal, but acknowledge that it is “highly speculative.”

verses.zh: 耶罗波安与他列祖以色列诸王同睡。他儿子撒迦利雅接续他作王。
verses.en: Jeroboam passed away[NOTE:1] and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.[NOTE:2] His son Zechariah replaced him as king.
notes: Heb “lay down with his fathers.”

The MT has simply “with the kings of Israel,” which appears to stand in apposition to the immediately preceding “with his fathers.” But it is likely that the words “and he was buried in Samaria” have been accidentally omitted from the text. See 13:13 and 14:16.
